title: The verifying constructor, and what Validation must and must not check
description:
VerifiedToken::verify, in hire-attestors/src/claim.rs, beside nothing else -- the type's own doc comment says the constructor lives next to the JWKS cache and nowhere else, and the reason is that a verified path an attestor may choose is a convention the next attestor omits.

TAKES A JWKS, DOES NOT FETCH ONE. persona-qbnm.7.3 owns the fetch. This is what makes the cryptography testable offline, the same split that made the gpg verifier testable with no gpg installed (see ChallengeSignature::verify_openpgp_against).

BUILDS THE TYPE AS 7e1bcde DEFINED IT: issuer_domain from the verified iss, verified_at stamped here, authenticated_at from the token's auth_time or None when it is absent. Never SystemTime::now() and never iat for authenticated_at -- the field's doc comment explains why, and both arms of the resulting tier are already tested.

WHAT Validation MUST NOT DO, and this is the part that will be got wrong: an ID token's `aud` is the OAuth CLIENT ID of whatever obtained it -- gcloud's, or the Azure CLI's -- and has nothing to do with the audience the consumer asked hired for. Validating aud against the consumer's audience refuses every real token; validating it against a hardcoded client id hardcodes somebody else's application. Decide deliberately whether aud is checked at all, and record it. hire-grpc/src/service.rs is the local precedent for the rest of the Validation config, and it now sets leeway explicitly rather than inheriting 60 (persona-yzl8) -- do the same here and for the same reason.

ALSO: restrict the accepted algorithms to what the JWKS actually contains, so a token declaring alg=none or a symmetric alg cannot select its own verifier. jsonwebtoken refuses alg=none, but the algorithm list is a Validation field and leaving it at the default is the same class of mistake as leaving leeway at 60.
acceptance_criteria: A token verifies against a supplied JWKS with no network; auth_time present and absent both produce the documented tier; the aud and algorithm decisions are recorded in the doc comment.
